questions.question_text: What is the equation of the tangent to $y = 2x^2 - 5x + 3$ at $x = 2$ in gradient–intercept form?

options.why: Used the positive y-value directly on the right-hand side without subtracting.
Subtracted the coordinates in reverse order when expanding the point-gradient form.
Used the linear coefficient of x as the gradient instead of evaluating the derivative.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^3 - 4x + 1$ at the point $(1, -2)$, written in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

options.why: Made a sign error when moving the constant term to the left-hand side.
Used a positive tangent gradient of 1 instead of negative 1.
Added rather than subtracted the negative y-coordinate in point-gradient form.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the normal to $y = x^2 - 2x + 4$ at the point $(2, 4)$ in gradient–intercept form.

options.why: Found the equation of the tangent instead of the normal.
Subtracted rather than added 1 when expanding the point-gradient bracket.
Used the reciprocal of the tangent gradient without the negative sign.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the normal to $y = 2x^2 - 3x - 2$ at $x = 1$ in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

options.why: Made a sign error when collecting constant terms on the left side.
Found the general form of the tangent line rather than the normal line.
Subtracted the y-coordinate with incorrect sign in point-gradient form.

questions.question_text: What is the equation of the normal to $y = 3 + 4x - x^2$ at its turning point $(2, 7)$?

options.why: Gave the equation of the horizontal tangent rather than the normal.
Confused the x-coordinate of the vertical line with a horizontal line equation.
Used the y-coordinate instead of the x-coordinate for the vertical line equation.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(x) = 4 - 2x$
$m = f'(2) = 4 - 2(2) = 0$
The tangent is the horizontal line $y = 7$.
The normal is the vertical line perpendicular to it through $(2, 7)$, which is $x = 2$.

questions.question_text:
The tangent to $y = x^2 - 2x$ at $x = 3$ cuts the $x$-axis at point $A$ and the $y$-axis at point $B$.
What is the area of $\triangle OAB$?

options.why: Forgot to multiply by one half in the triangle area formula.
Used the curve y-value of 3 instead of the tangent y-intercept of 9.
Halved the product of the x-intercept and curve y-value instead of the y-intercept.

questions.solution_text:
$y_1 = (3)^2 - 2(3) = 3$
$f'(x) = 2x - 2$
$m = f'(3) = 2(3) - 2 = 4$
$y - 3 = 4(x - 3)$
$y = 4x - 9$
At $A$ ($y = 0$): $4x - 9 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{9}{4} \implies A\left(\dfrac{9}{4}, 0\right)$
At $B$ ($x = 0$): $y = -9 \implies B(0, -9)$
$\text{Area of } \triangle OAB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{9}{4} \times 9 = \dfrac{81}{8}$

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the tangent to $y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 5$ at $x = 3$, written in general form $ax + by + c = 0$.

options.why: Differentiated $-3x^2$ as $-6$ instead of $-6x$, giving $f'(3) = 27 - 6 = 21$.
Used $y - 5 = 9(x + 3)$, taking the sign of the $x$-coordinate wrongly in point-gradient form.
Made both slips: differentiated $-3x^2$ as $-6$ and then substituted $x + 3$ instead of $x - 3$.

questions.question_text:
The parabola $y = x^2 + kx + 3$ has a normal with equation $x + 4y - 12 = 0$ at the point $(0, 3)$ on the curve.
What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Applied the negative sign incorrectly when finding the tangent gradient.
Equated the derivative directly to the normal gradient instead of negative reciprocal.
Took the reciprocal without changing the sign from the normal gradient.

questions.solution_text:
$x + 4y - 12 = 0 \implies 4y = -x + 12 \implies y = -\dfrac{1}{4}x + 3$
$\text{Normal gradient } m_{\perp} = -\dfrac{1}{4} \implies \text{tangent gradient } m = 4$
$f'(x) = 2x + k$
$f'(0) = 2(0) + k = k$
$k = 4$

questions.question_text:
The curve has equation $y=x^2+2x+1$ and the green line is tangent to the curve at $(-2,1)$.
What are the coordinates of point Q, where the tangent crosses the x-axis?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.55]\draw[->] (-4,0)--(2,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,-4)--(0,4) node[above] {$y$};\draw[domain=-3.5:1,smooth,thick] plot (\x,{\x*\x+2*\x+1});\draw[domain=-3.5:1,smooth,thick,green] plot (\x,{-2*\x-3});\fill (-2,1) circle (2pt);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Uses an incorrect tangent gradient or intercept calculation.
Confuses the tangency x-coordinate with the tangent's x-intercept.
Does not use the tangent gradient at the specified point.

questions.solution_text: The gradient is $dy/dx=2x+2$, so at $x=-2$ it is $-2$. The tangent is $y-1=-2(x+2)$, or $y=-2x-3$. Setting $y=0$ gives $x=-3/2$, so Q is $(-1.5,0)$.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the normal to $y=10x-x^3+2$ at the point $(2,14)$.

options.why: Uses the tangent gradient with an incorrect point form.
Uses the wrong sign for the negative reciprocal of the tangent gradient.
Uses the wrong intercept form and the wrong normal gradient.

questions.solution_text: The tangent gradient is $y'=10-3x^2=-2$ at $x=2$. The normal gradient is $\frac12$, so the equation through $(2,14)$ is $y-14=\frac12(x-2)$.
